messages:
maya: @acme_ops thanks for the report — can you share the request_id and a curl repro? We're seeing structured output validation failures on your function/tool call.

acme_ops: request_id=01F8Z9ABCDEF12345. Here's the minimal curl we've been using (we're hitting /v1/responses with function_call):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r-redwood","input":"compute summary","tool_call":{"name":"summarize","arguments":{"text":"..."}}}'
```

devon: quick question — is the schema you're passing in the request body or is this the server-side expected schema? also last 4 of the req id?

acme_ops: schema is server-side (we linked a JSON schema in our model config). last 4 = 2345. The error we see in our app: "ValidationError: tool_call.response.output: expected object, got string". Happens intermittently (maybe 1-2% of calls).

maya: can you run this variant which logs the raw response from the Redwood API (adds raw_response=true) and paste the exact body you receive? it will help us see whether the runtime is returning a stringified JSON or actual object.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r-redwood","input":"compute summary","raw_response":true,"tool_call":{"name":"summarize","arguments":{"text":"..."}}}'
```

acme_ops: pasted raw body below (redacted):
```json
{
  "id": "resp_01F8Z9ABCDEF12345",
  "object": "response",
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "summarize",
    "response": {
      "output": "{\"summary\": \"Short summary text\"}"
    }
  }
}
```

eli: that matches what my quick log check shows from runtime: sometimes we see the function output marshalled as a JSON string rather than an object. log snippet: `ERROR runtime: validation failed: path '.tool_call.response.output' expected object got string (req=01F8Z9ABCDEF12345)`. looking at the worker that handled that req it returned a 200 but with output as a serialized string.

jen-sre: adding SRE context — I see a couple of related warnings in the node that handled that batch around 2026-09-03T21:10:12Z: `kv-cache: miss; fallthrough to model`; and `worker: kafka-retry 2/3`. could be a race during async post-processing where we call JSON.stringify twice.

devon: can you share the exact tool definition that the runtime was given? specifically the expected schema for `tool_call.response.output`. we need to reproduce locally.

acme_ops: our tool schema (server-side) expects: `{"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}`. we don't stringify anything client-side.

maya: thanks. devon/eli will try to reproduce locally with a small harness. @acme_ops, can you upload the debug bundle from the failing run? the debug bundle agent link is below — it collects request headers, a sample of the model response, and the worker logs for the request_id.

support-bot: A debug bundle request has been created: https://internal.redwood/debug-bundles/new?req=01F8Z9ABCDEF12345 — please upload the zipped bundle there; token valid 24h.

acme_ops: uploaded bundle (link: https://acme.s3/redwood/debug-01F8Z9ABCDEF12345.zip). let us know if you need more.

devon: thanks — I reproduced with a small harness by sending a simulated function that returns "{\"summary\": \"x\"}" as a string when the model emits a single-line tool response. reduced repro attached:```json
{
  "model":"gpt-4r-redwood-sim",
  "tool_output":"{\"summary\": \"x\"}"
}
```

eli: root cause hypothesis: when the model emits a tool call whose content type is ambiguous (plain text that happens to be JSON), we sometimes leave it as a raw string. downstream serializer then wraps it again. two fixes: (1) on the runtime side, try to detect safe JSON strings and parse them before validation; (2) ensure our tool schema validation accepts both string and object (with warning) for a short term fallback.

maya: action items:
- devon/eli: implement a deterministic parse-and-validate step in runtime (dev branch: fix/toolcall-coerce).
- jen-sre: monitor for any increase in 5xx or latency from the added parse step.
- support: provide customer workaround (client-side) and ETA.

devon: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 (adds coercion for stringified JSON when schema expects object). test plan included.

eli: deployed a canary to staging that coerces strings -> try JSON.parse if it looks like JSON; fixed ~ 98% of cases in our sim. no meaningful latency bump (p95 +3ms).

maya: @acme_ops workaround — for now we recommend unwrapping stringified outputs in your client before schema validation: if typeof output === 'string' try JSON.parse(output) and only fail if parse throws. we know that's not ideal but reduces errors until runtime patch is deployed.

acme_ops: we'll add the client-side parse. appreciate the quick turnaround. please ping when the patch is in prod so we can remove the workaround.

devon: ETA for prod rollout: 24h after tests pass, post-rollout I'll send the prod run request_id.

support-bot: Incident INC-3421 updated: status=investigating, assignees=[maya, devon, eli], priority=P2.

maya: leaving notes for the customer: pinned links -> debug bundle, reduced repro, and the temporary client-side snippet. once prod patch lands we'll follow up with a final postmortem and regression test added to the suite. :thumbsup:
